scenes.visual: Title card 'Watch the Per-Capita Rate' over a faint grid. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: N (population size or density) in WHITE; the per-capita rate and any per-capita line in TEAL; the carrying capacity K as a GOLD dashed line; total growth dN/dt in ORANGE. Dark navy background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Curves are computed from the model with r = 0.2 per day, K = 1,000, N0 = 100 and labelled 'computed'; cartoons and anything not computed are labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Here is a small population, and the rate it is growing at right now. Will tomorrow's rate be the same, or faster?
scenes.visual: A cluster of 100 small WHITE animal icons (schematic). A TEAL-outlined tag reads 'N = 100; growth rate now: about 20 per day'. A question mark hovers over a calendar that flips to 'tomorrow?'.
scenes.narration: Here is a small population, and the rate it is growing at right now. Will tomorrow's rate be the same, or faster?

scenes.tts: Look at one individual. Over a day it may give birth, and it may die. Births minus deaths, per individual, is the per-capita rate.
scenes.visual: Zoom to one WHITE icon. A small '+ births' arrow and a '- deaths' arrow; they merge into a TEAL badge 'per-capita rate = births - deaths, per individual'.
scenes.narration: Look at one individual. Over a day it may give birth, and it may die. Births minus deaths, per individual, is the per-capita rate.

scenes.tts: Multiply that per-capita rate by the population size, en. In a closed population, with no one moving in or out, that product is the population's growth. This one rule runs the whole film.
scenes.caption: Multiply that per-capita rate by the population size, N. In a closed population, with no one moving in or out, that product is the population's growth. This one rule runs the whole film.
scenes.visual: The TEAL badge slides into an on-screen rule: 'growth = per-capita rate x N', with N in WHITE and 'growth' in ORANGE, and a small subtitle 'closed population: no one moves in or out'. It parks at the top of the screen for the rest of the film.
scenes.narration: Multiply that per-capita rate by the population size, N. In a closed population, with no one moving in or out, that product is the population's growth. This one rule runs the whole film.

scenes.tts: On the left, plot the per-capita rate against en. First, hold it flat, the same value at every size.
scenes.caption: On the left, plot the per-capita rate against N. First, hold it flat, the same value at every size.
scenes.visual: Two panels appear. Left: x axis 'N' 0 to 1,200, y axis 'per-capita rate (per day)' -0.05 to 0.25; a flat TEAL line at 0.2 draws across, labelled 'r = 0.2 per day'. Right: empty axes, x 'time (days)' 0 to 20, y 'N' 0 to 1,200.
scenes.narration: On the left, plot the per-capita rate against N. First, hold it flat, the same value at every size.

scenes.tts: Now watch the right panel. Each newcomer soon adds newcomers of its own. So each day's gain is bigger than the day before.
scenes.visual: Right panel: a WHITE curve N = 100 e^(0.2t) (computed) grows from day 0. Small WHITE bars under the curve show each day's gain, each taller than the last; tags '+22', '+27', '+33' appear on the first three bars.
scenes.narration: Now watch the right panel. Each newcomer soon adds newcomers of its own. So each day's gain is bigger than the day before.

scenes.tts: By day ten, the population is far above what steady adding would give. This compounding is exponential growth, a J-shaped curve.
scenes.visual: Two markers on the right panel at day 10: a faint dashed line labelled '300 if it added 20 a day' and the WHITE curve's point labelled '739 (computed)'. Then the curve continues steeply off the top of the panel; label 'J-curve: exponential'.
scenes.narration: By day ten, the population is far above what steady adding would give. This compounding is exponential growth, a J-shaped curve.

scenes.tts: No real population keeps this up. As numbers rise, each individual gets less food, space or shelter. Births fall, or deaths rise.
scenes.visual: The 100 icons multiply until they crowd the frame; small food and shelter icons thin out between them (schematic). On the left panel, a downward arrow hovers over the TEAL line.
scenes.narration: No real population keeps this up. As numbers rise, each individual gets less food, space or shelter. Births fall, or deaths rise.

scenes.tts: So tilt the line. Let the per-capita rate fall as en rises. The logistic model assumes it falls in a straight line.
scenes.caption: So tilt the line. Let the per-capita rate fall as N rises. The logistic model assumes it falls in a straight line.
scenes.visual: Left panel: the flat TEAL line pivots at its left end (0.2 at N = 0) and tilts down. Label 'logistic: an assumed straight line'.
scenes.narration: So tilt the line. Let the per-capita rate fall as N rises. The logistic model assumes it falls in a straight line.

scenes.tts: The line hits zero at a size called kay, the carrying capacity. There, births balance deaths on average, so the per-capita rate is zero.
scenes.caption: The line hits zero at a size called K, the carrying capacity. There, births balance deaths on average, so the per-capita rate is zero.
scenes.visual: Where the tilted TEAL line crosses zero, a GOLD dashed vertical marker drops at N = 1,000, labelled 'K = 1,000'. On the right panel, a matching GOLD dashed horizontal line appears at N = 1,000.
scenes.narration: The line hits zero at a size called K, the carrying capacity. There, births balance deaths on average, so the per-capita rate is zero.

scenes.tts: Redraw the right panel with the falling line. The curve rises, steepens, then bends and levels off toward kay. That is the S-shaped curve.
scenes.caption: Redraw the right panel with the falling line. The curve rises, steepens, then bends and levels off toward K. That is the S-shaped curve.
scenes.visual: Right panel: the J-curve fades to a faint ghost; a WHITE logistic curve (computed) draws from 100, through about 451 at day 10, and flattens under the GOLD dashed K line by day 30 (extend the axis to 30 days). Label 'S-curve: logistic'.
scenes.narration: Redraw the right panel with the falling line. The curve rises, steepens, then bends and levels off toward K. That is the S-shaped curve.

scenes.tts: Here is a question before we go on. On this S-curve, at what size is the population adding the most individuals per day?
scenes.visual: The WHITE S-curve pulses. Three tags float beside it: 'when N is small', 'halfway to K', 'right at K'.
scenes.narration: Here is a question before we go on. On this S-curve, at what size is the population adding the most individuals per day?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown ring; caption 'Predict: where does the population add the most per day?'.

scenes.tts: Halfway to kay. When the population is small, each individual adds a lot, but there are few of them. Near kay, there are many, each adding little.
scenes.caption: Halfway to K. When the population is small, each individual adds a lot, but there are few of them. Near K, there are many, each adding little.
scenes.visual: The 'halfway to K' tag lights. Left panel: a sliding cursor on the TEAL line shows a tall rate with few WHITE icons at low N, then a short rate with many icons near K.
scenes.narration: Halfway to K. When the population is small, each individual adds a lot, but there are few of them. Near K, there are many, each adding little.

scenes.tts: Multiply the two at every size and plot the product in orange. It makes a hump, highest at half of kay. That is where the S-curve is steepest.
scenes.caption: Multiply the two at every size and plot the product in orange. It makes a hump, highest at half of K. That is where the S-curve is steepest.
scenes.visual: A third panel under the left one: x axis 'N' 0 to 1,000, y axis 'total growth (individuals per day)'; an ORANGE parabola (computed) rises to a peak at N = 500 and returns to 0 at K. A dotted link joins the hump's peak to the steepest point of the S-curve, labelled 'K/2 = 500'. On-screen: 'peak = 50 per day'.
scenes.narration: Multiply the two at every size and plot the product in orange. It makes a hump, highest at half of K. That is where the S-curve is steepest.

scenes.tts: At kay, the hump comes back down to zero. Growth stops there because each individual's per-capita rate has fallen to zero.
scenes.caption: At K, the hump comes back down to zero. Growth stops there because each individual's per-capita rate has fallen to zero.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE hump's right end touches zero at the GOLD K marker; the TEAL line's zero crossing is at the same point. Both flash once.
scenes.narration: At K, the hump comes back down to zero. Growth stops there because each individual's per-capita rate has fallen to zero.

scenes.tts: So the whole story sits in one teal line. Hold it flat, and growth compounds. Let it fall to zero, and growth stops at kay.
scenes.caption: So the whole story sits in one teal line. Hold it flat, and growth compounds. Let it fall to zero, and growth stops at K.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, the flat TEAL line beside the J-curve; right, the tilted TEAL line beside the S-curve and the ORANGE hump. The rule 'growth = per-capita rate x N' stays at top.
scenes.narration: So the whole story sits in one teal line. Hold it flat, and growth compounds. Let it fall to zero, and growth stops at K.

scenes.tts: The straight line is the model's assumption, not a measurement. Whether real populations have a falling line must be tested in the field.
scenes.visual: The tilted TEAL line gets a stamp 'assumption'. A small field-notebook icon and a question mark appear beside it, labelled 'measure it'.
scenes.narration: The straight line is the model's assumption, not a measurement. Whether real populations have a falling line must be tested in the field.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'Growth stops where the per-capita rate falls to zero: at K.'
